rounds.text: Rashi Peripherals Ltd is trading at a compelling valuation with a P/E ratio of just 17x [E1], which sits below the sector benchmark of 21.18x [E6], while offering exceptional top-line and bottom-line momentum featuring 40% TTM sales growth [E16] and 50% TTM profit growth [E19]. Fundamental quality metrics validate this operating strength, as the company delivers a ROCE of 17.0% [E12] and an ROA of 6.1%, outperforming sector benchmarks of 11.3% and 5.01% respectively [E8, E10], backed by a rules-based screen score of 93 out of 100 indicating a high-confidence buy [E56]. Furthermore, intrinsic value models estimate a significant margin of safety [E41], with a reverse DCF revealing that the current market price only prices in a modest 5.8% earnings growth compared to a base case expectation of 16.0% [E42], all reinforced by a supportive IT sector tailwind score of +0.67 [E64]. Conceded: cash conversion stands at 0.40x with operating cash flow representing only 41% of operating profit [E28, E31], institutional money flow is negative [E39], and operating margins remain flat at 3% [E24].

The fundamental concern with Rashi Peripherals Ltd is a severe disconnect between reported earnings and actual cash generation, highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.40x where operating cash flow accounts for only 41% of operating profit [E28, E31]. This divergence suggests aggressive accruals or trapped working capital, which is compounded by rising debt obligations as total borrowings increased to Rs 991 Cr [E34]. Institutional conviction is simultaneously eroding, evidenced by a drop in domestic institutional holdings from 14.41% to 12.68% and an overall negative money flow signal [E38, E39]. Furthermore, operating margins remain flat at 3% with an inconsistent trend [E24, E26], while longer-term return on equity has been flagged as low at 13.2% over a three-year period [E55]. Speculative froth is also evident as recent price growth has outpaced profit growth by 122%, meaning market expectations are running dangerously ahead of fundamental delivery [E52]. Conceded: [E14], [E16], [E19].

While the bear highlights a low cash conversion ratio of 0.40x for March 2026 [E28], this must be viewed alongside a healthy operating cash flow of Rs 114 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs 106 Cr achieved in the same period [E29, E30]. Conceded: [E34]. Although domestic institutional holdings saw a decrease [E38], foreign institutional investors actually increased their stake to 3.27% from 1.63%, and promoter ownership rose to 64.04% [E36, E37]. The concern over flat operating margins at 3% [E24] is thoroughly countered by explosive top-line and bottom-line expansion, including a 40% TTM sales growth and a 50% TTM profit growth [E16, E19]. Finally, while the bear points to past three-year ROE [E55], the company's current ROCE of 15.84% comfortably beats the sector benchmark of 11.3% [E10], and the rules-based screen awards the stock a high-confidence BUY score of 93 out of 100 [E56].

Conceded: [E29, E30, E36, E37]. While the bull celebrates cash generation, operating cash flow for March 2026 was only 41% of operating profit, exposing a wide and troubling gap between reported accounting profits and actual cash realized [E28, E31]. The bull cites rapid sales and profit expansion [E16, E19], but ignores that operating margins remain stuck at a meager 3% with an inconsistent trend over the last year [E24, E26, E27]. Conceded: [E10]. Although the current ROCE beats sector benchmarks, the company's historical three-year return on equity is flagged as a direct negative by filed statements at a low 13.2% [E55]. Furthermore, despite the bull's optimism, domestic institutions reduced their holdings [E38], contributing to an overall institutional outflow and negative money flow signal of 2.28 percentage points [E39, E61]. Finally, the scanX signal engine warns that recent price growth exceeds profit growth by 122%, proving that market expectations are running dangerously ahead of actual business delivery [E52].

Conceded: [E28, E31]. While cash conversion dipped in March 2026, the business still produced substantial absolute liquidity with ₹ 114 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹ 106 Cr in free cash flow [E29, E30]. The bear worries about a stagnant 3% operating margin [E24, E26, E27], but ignores that this model drives exceptional top-line and bottom-line velocity, posting 40% trailing sales growth and 50% trailing profit growth that far outpace the sector medians of 14.3% and 11.1% [E16, E19, E65, E66]. Conceded: [E38, E39, E61]. Despite those institutional reductions, overall promoter confidence rose alongside foreign institutional holdings, which increased from 1.63% to 3.27% [E36, E37].

Conceded: [E29, E30]. While absolute cash generation of ₹ 114 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹ 106 Cr in free cash flow occurred [E29, E30], the underlying efficiency remains heavily impaired as operating cash flow was only 41% of operating profit, exposing a wide and dangerous gap where profits run far ahead of actual cash collection due to receivables or accruals [E28, E31]. The bull celebrates trailing sales and profit velocities of 40% and 50% [E16, E19], but this high-octane growth masks a dangerously stagnant operating margin anchored at a meager 3% with an inconsistent trend over the last year [E24, E26, E27]. Furthermore, the bull's attempt to downplay institutional selling by pointing to rising foreign holdings [E37] ignores the broader reality of negative money flow and a steep 1.73 percentage point reduction in domestic institutional holdings, confirming that smart money is actively retreating from the name [E38, E39, E61]. Finally, the massive 177% twelve-month price return running rampant over a low 13.2% three-year ROE [E47, E55] reinforces the automated warning that price growth exceeds profit growth by 122%, proving that expectations are violently running ahead of delivery [E52].
